jobs.title: Director Media Analytics
jobs.description:
Overview

L9 Director Media Analytics

What you'll be doing

The Marketing and Client Solutions Decision Sciences ( Growth) team is at the center of our Media

practice, strategy and innovation at CIBC. Its sole focus is to efficiently drive growth in reach and

conversions through efficient media investments that are data driven. We work across different

enterprise teams at CIBC and Simplii helping them understand and serve our clients and Canadians

better each day. We apply best practices in marketing measurement, descriptive and predictive analysis,

machine learning, artificial intelligence and leverage the latest in big data technology platforms.

Reporting into the COE Lead for Marketing and Client solutions within AI Data and Analytics, this role is

responsible for leading a Media decision sciences practice, delivering on strategic priorities, managing

and maintaining team operations and senior stakeholder relationships, equipping the Media Ops teams

with high quality and timely data and insights to continuously optimize our Media. This Director will

lead, manage and mentor a small team of Junior and Media scientists. This role requires a hands-on

approach to solving problems, planning and managing change related to all aspects of marketing

sciences delivery.

At CIBC we enable the work environment most optimal for you to thrive in your role you’ll have the

flexibility to manage your work activities within a hybrid work arrangement where you’ll spend 1-3 days

per week on-site, while other days will be remote.

How You Will Succeed

Champion media analytics as a strategic growth driver — Serve as the trusted analytics partner to

marketing, retail, wealth, and distribution leaders by translating business priorities into clear media

measurement, experimentation, and optimization strategies. Ensure solutions are practical, scalable, and

aligned to business outcomes.

Lead measurement, experimentation, and optimization across the media ecosystem — Oversee

the design, implementation, and ongoing evaluation of analytics frameworks, models, and test-and-learn

programs that improve media effectiveness. Guide the team in applying advanced analytics, AI/ML, and

emerging GenAI capabilities to both structured and unstructured data, with a strong focus on campaign

performance, attribution, audience insights, and investment optimization.

Deliver end-to-end analytical solutions — Lead work from problem definition and methodology

through execution, validation, monitoring, and refinement. Continuously evolve approaches as business

needs shift, new channels emerge, or performance insights suggest optimization opportunities.

Build a high-performing analytics function — Lead, coach, and develop a strong team of media

analytics professionals. Hire and nurture talent with the right blend of analytical rigor, business acumen,

and media expertise. Set clear expectations, remove barriers, and ensure the team is aligned to business

priorities and enterprise goals.

Embed responsible, effective analytics practices — Foster high standards in measurement design,

data quality, experimentation discipline, and responsible AI use. Ensure the team’s work adheres to

relevant policies, governance standards, and best practices while maintaining credibility with partners

across the organization.

Who You Are

You are a media analytics leader first — You bring strong command of the media landscape and

understand how to connect channels, audiences, and investments to measurable business outcomes. You

are fluent in media effectiveness, incrementality, attribution, testing, and optimization.

You combine craft expertise with strategic thinking — You know how to move from business

question to analytical approach to actionable recommendation. You are comfortable shaping

measurement strategies that inform planning, improve performance, and support better investment

decisions.

You are highly analytical and experimentally minded — You have deep experience applying

advanced analytics to marketing and media use cases, including forecasting, audience analysis, causal

measurement, optimization, and performance diagnostics. You understand how to structure rigorous

experiments and use evidence to guide decisions.

You are digitally and technically fluent — You are comfortable working with modern analytics and

data science tools such as Python, SQL, Pandas, scikit-learn, and cloud-based data environments. You can

partner effectively with technical teams while staying focused on business relevance and usability.

You are an effective translator between technical and business teams — You can turn complex

analytical concepts into clear, compelling narratives for senior stakeholders. You know how to influence

decisions, build trust, and bring partners along in environments with complexity and ambiguity.

You are a strong people leader — You lead with clarity, accountability, and empathy. You develop

talent, elevate team capability, and create an inclusive environment where high performance and

collaboration go hand in hand.

You understand applied AI in a marketing context — You have experience using traditional AI/ML

techniques and an appreciation for where GenAI can enhance workflows, insight generation, and

decision support. You are thoughtful about where these tools add value and where rigor in

measurement must remain paramount.

You bring strong business and industry judgment — Experience in marketing, media, or sales

analytics is essential, and financial services experience is a strong asset. You understand how to operate

in a regulated, complex environment while still driving innovation and impact.

You are well-credentialed and credible — You bring advanced academic training in analytics,

statistics, economics, mathematics, computer science, engineering, or a related discipline, along with a

track record of delivering large, high-impact analytical initiatives.

What you need to know

CIBC is committed to creating an inclusive environment where all team members and clients feel

like they belong. We seek applicants with a wide range of abilities and we provide an accessible

candidate experience. If you need accommodation, please contact Mailbox.careers

carrieres@cibc.com

You need to be legally eligible to work at the location(s) specified above and, where applicable,

must have a valid work or study permit

We may ask you to complete an attribute-based assessment and other skills tests (such as

simulation, coding, French proficiency, MS Office). Our goal for the application process is to get

to know more about you, all that you have to offer, and give you the opportunity to learn more

jobs.title: Senior Director, Enterprise Architecture - Corporate Technology Services
jobs.description:
Accelerate your success at Colliers.

Why Colliers?

As one of Canada’s leading commercial real estate services firms, we are driven by our mission to accelerate success for our people, clients, and communities.

A career at Colliers gives you the opportunity to make an impact, advance your career, and collaborate with top-tier talent. Don’t just take our word for it – we’ve been recognized as a top employer on a number of prestigious lists, including Best Workplaces in Canada, Best Workplaces with Most Trusted Executive Teams, among others.

Toronto, ON / Vancouver, BC, Hybrid

About The Role

As Global Domain Enterprise Architect, Corporate Technology Systems within our Global Enterprise Architecture organization, you’ll define the global architectural direction for the technology platforms supporting Colliers’ corporate functions. You’ll partner with business and technology leaders to simplify and modernize our global technology landscape, establish scalable standards, and ensure major technology investments translate into sustainable business outcomes. Support global time zones: Work closely with stakeholders across Pacific and APAC regions, with flexibility to adjust working hours on most days as business needs require.

Lead global enterprise architecture: Define current-state, target-state, and transition architectures, roadmaps, principles, and standards across ERP, Finance, HCM, Procurement, CRM/MarTech, Legal, Risk & Compliance, ECM, and other corporate platforms.
Drive modernization and simplification: Lead application portfolio rationalization and recommend where platforms should be standardized, modernized, consolidated, replaced, or retired to reduce technical debt and complexity.
Shape strategic technology investments: Provide architecture leadership for major transformation initiatives, evaluating SaaS and enterprise platforms against business value, integration, data, security, scalability, total cost, and long-term strategic fit.
Advance AI, data, and integration strategy: Establish scalable patterns for enterprise data, APIs, integration, automation, AI, identity, and shared services while embedding security, privacy, governance, and regulatory requirements.
Collaborate across the global enterprise: Partner with senior business leaders, Product, Data & AI, Cloud & DevOps, Cybersecurity, Integration, Legal, Procurement, Risk, and strategic vendors to turn architecture strategy into executable outcomes.

What You Bring

Education: Degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, Business, or a related discipline preferred.
12+ years of relevant experience: Significant experience in enterprise architecture, domain architecture, technology strategy, or large-scale transformation within complex global or federated organizations.
Enterprise platform architecture expertise: Demonstrated experience architecting and modernizing complex technology portfolios, including experience across at least two of the following three domains: Finance/ERP, HR/HCM, and CRM/MarTech.
Strong technical and transformation expertise: Deep understanding of SaaS platforms, application rationalization, enterprise integration, APIs, data architecture, cloud, cybersecurity, identity, AI/automation, and executable transition roadmaps.
Executive influence and communication: Proven ability to advise senior executives, challenge vendor and solution assumptions, and translate complex architectural decisions into clear business outcomes while remaining technically credible with architecture and engineering teams.

What We Offer

Innovative projects:
Work on cutting-edge initiatives that shape our communities, drive our growth, and make a tangible impact.

Career growth:
Advance your career and achieve your goals with industry-leading training and development programs.

Competitive benefits & compensation:
Enjoy a comprehensive and flexible benefits package along with competitive compensation that rewards your contributions and supports your well-being.

Collaborative culture:
Join our enterprising team where innovation thrives, collaboration is key, and our people are empowered to be their authentic selves and do their best work.

Diversity, Equity & Inclusion:
Our robust North American Diversity & Inclusion Program features eight Employee Resource Groups (ERGs), where you can connect, learn, and contribute to a diverse and supportive community. Learn more: https://www.collierscanada.com/en-ca/careers/diversity-and-inclusion

Global network
: Join a global team of 28,000 professionals across 70 countries, where you'll expand your network and learn from experts in a dynamic international community. Accelerate your career and enhance your expertise as you connect and collaborate with top talent around the world.

Applicants must be currently authorized to work in Canada on a full-time basis. The employer will not sponsor applicants for work visas.

Direct applicants only please, no agencies.

Colliers is an equal opportunity employer and values diversity in its workforce. Colliers encourages applications from all qualified individuals and will accommodate applicants' disability-related needs, up to the point of undue hardship, throughout all stages of the recruitment and selection process. If you require a disability-related accommodation to participate in the recruitment process, please contact the recruitment team by email at careers@colliers.com.

jobs.title: Individual Insurance Pricing and Finance VP
jobs.description:
At Equitable, we believe work should be a place where you feel supported, inspired, and empowered to grow. In our caring and collaborative environment, your curiosity is encouraged, your passion is recognized, and your contributions truly matter. Together, we create meaningful impact, for our clients, our communities, and each other.

The Opportunity:
  At Equitable, we believe great things happen when we work together. We’re a Canadian mutual company driven by purpose - putting people first and helping Canadians protect today and prepare for tomorrow. If you’re passionate about making a difference and growing your career in an inclusive and collaborative environment, we’d love to hear from you.

Our culture is built on care, passion and curiosity. We put people above all else, strive to be our best and welcome new ideas to deliver positive outcomes.

We are looking for an Individual Pricing and Finance Vice-President to lead the Actuarial and Finance functions of our Individual Insurance division. This role will play a central role in driving the growth and profitability of these functions.

Join one of the region’s top employers and be part of something that truly makes a difference.

Work Arrangements:
This is a hybrid role. You will work in our office in Waterloo, ON a minimum of two (2) assigned, consecutive days every other week, plus a fifth (5th) assigned day per month. You are welcome to work from the office more than the minimum requirement and there may be some roles that are required to work in our office more than the minimum requirement.

Reports To:
Executive Vice President, Individual Insurance

Department:
Individual Insurance

Term:
Permanent Full-Time

What you’ll do:

Participate with other senior leaders in setting the vision, strategies and priorities for the division in alignment with corporate goals and objectives
Direct the development of financial plans for the division to operationalize strategic goals, overseeing the monitoring and reporting results, explaining changes in performance and taking or recommending corrective action
Support product development, in partnership with the AVP of Marketing, with a specific focus on ensuring growth strategies will be profitable and that risks are identified and managed
Oversee product pricing, reinsurance arrangements, dividend scale reviews, and compensation arrangements for all levels of distribution (internal and external), and monitoring their execution to achieve growth and profitability goals
Provide direction to the Individual Insurance leadership team with respect to opportunities and challenges in attainment of the financial plan
Oversee a production team responsible for large case quotes, exception requests and other underwriting and distribution support from the pricing team
Lead a finance team with accountability for setting, managing, and monitoring budgets, sales targets and a number of financial reports and metrics
Participate as a member of the Actuarial Student Executive Committee which oversees the actuarial student program and the actuarial community for the organization
Develop internal and external relationships to stay on top of trends in markets, products, distribution, accounting and tax, capital, investments, actuarial standards and practices, etc. so that actions can be taken proactively
Sponsor and / or participate on PMO steering committees for product, operational or financial projects where Pricing or Finance are stakeholders
Lead a team of data scientists and data analysts in developing predictive modeling to increase productivity in underwriting and operations and developing dashboards to support oversight of the business unit’s key performance and productivity metrics
Lead the advisor and sales practices risk monitoring role and function, ensuring that robust controls and processes are in place to protect the integrity of our distribution, identify advisors or sales practices that do not meet our standards and ensure that clients are treated fairly

What you’ll bring:

At least 15 years insurance experience, including at least 5 years in Individual Insurance and at least 5 years in a leadership role
FSA and/or FCIA designations required
Advanced knowledge of the individual life and health insurance business including product design, pricing and valuation methodologies and assumptions, asset-liability management techniques, financial reporting standards, regulatory capital requirements, policyholder taxation and sales/marketing concepts for family and advanced markets
Knowledge of AXIS software
Impeccable judgement and ability to make sound decisions in a fast paced, dynamic setting
Ability to coach and mentor AVP and director level staff (actuaries, accountants and data scientists) in both their professional and leadership development
Advanced skills in negotiation, influencing, and relationship-building
Excellent communication and presentation skills and ability to handle high-level executive and client interactions
Strong planning, project management and organization skills
Demonstrated ability to interact with team members of different disciplines including distribution, marketing, IT and Administration

What’s in it for you:

Career Growth: Regular learning sessions and development opportunities 
Total Rewards: Incentive pay, annual salary reviews, employer-paid benefits and pension matching 
Time Away: Competitive vacation plus one paid volunteer day each year
Flexibility: Healthy work-life balance with employee wellness always top of mind, complemented by a “dress for your day” approach

We’re committed to fair pay and an inclusive, accessible hiring experience. If you need accommodations or alternative formats at any stage, just reach out to us at careers@equitable.ca. We’re happy to help.

If you’re selected to move forward, our Talent Acquisition team will walk you through all the details of our total rewards program, so you know exactly what’s included. This position is open and we are excited to find the right person to join our team. Your base pay will be based on your skills, qualifications, experience and education.

At Equitable, your resume will be reviewed by real people and all hiring decisions are made by our recruiters and hiring managers. AI tools may be used to support administrative and productivity tasks throughout the recruitment process, but we believe that evaluating experience, skills, and talent potential requires meaningful human interaction.

As part of our commitment to maintaining a secure and trusted workplace, candidates selected to move forward in the recruitment process will be required to complete a background screening in accordance with company policy.

jobs.title: Alternatives Business Solutions – Private Equity, Managing Director
jobs.description:
Who We Are Looking For

State Street is seeking a Managing Director to lead Private Equity Business Solutions and Platform Strategy within Alternatives. This executive leadership role will be responsible for defining and executing the strategic vision for the Private Equity servicing platform, with a particular focus on Investran and the broader ecosystem of applications, workflows, integrations, controls, and operating model components that support the Alternatives business.

The successful candidate will serve as the primary business leader responsible for aligning technology capabilities, operational processes, data strategy, and client requirements to create a scalable, efficient, and modern Private Equity servicing platform. This individual will partner closely with Global Delivery, Technology, Product, Operations, Data Strategy, and Client Service teams to drive platform modernization, improve operational resiliency, and establish best practices across the Private Equity organization.

What You Will Be Responsible For

Platform Strategy & Transformation Leadership

Define and maintain the strategic roadmap for the Private Equity technology platform with Investran serving as a foundational component of the operating model.
Lead multi-year modernization initiatives focused on application rationalization, automation, workflow digitization, data quality, and platform integration.
Establish a future-state operating model that supports scalability, process standardization, and operational excellence across Private Equity servicing functions.
Drive the evaluation, prioritization, and execution of strategic business initiatives impacting accounting, investor services, allocations, reporting, workflow management, and data management capabilities.
Partner with Technology and Product teams to align investment priorities with business objectives and client requirements.

Investran Leadership & Governance

Act as the senior business owner and subject matter leader for Investran strategy, governance, and adoption across Private Equity operations.
Establish platform standards, governance frameworks, and operating procedures to ensure consistent utilization across regions and service teams.
Drive enhancements, integrations, controls, and automation opportunities surrounding Investran and supporting applications.
Lead business readiness activities for major platform upgrades, releases, conversions, and new functionality deployments.
Partner with operational teams to identify opportunities to reduce manual processing, improve data lineage, and increase straight-through processing.

Production Support & Operational Excellence

Provide executive oversight for Private Equity platform stability, service delivery effectiveness in collaboration with production support.
Establish proactive monitoring, issue management, escalation, and root cause analysis procedures to improve platform resiliency.
Collaborate with service delivery, operations, and technology teams to analyze production incidents and work to resolve recurring operational challenges.
Develop service metrics and operational reporting that provide transparency into platform health, risk exposure, and performance against objectives.
Champion continuous improvement initiatives that strengthen controls, reduce operational risk, and improve user experience

Best Practices, Controls & Model Office

Establish and maintain a Private Equity Model Office function focused on process optimization, controls, operational governance, and standardization.
Develop best practice frameworks for accounting operations, investor services, workflows, controls, onboarding, reconciliations, and reporting.
Proven ability to lead global, cross-functional teams in complex and highly regulated environments.

Education & Experience

Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Information Systems, Business Administration, or related field.
Advanced degree preferred.
15+ years of experience in Alternatives, Asset Servicing, Private Equity, Fund Administration, Financial Technology, or related disciplines.
Significant leadership experience overseeing technology strategy, business transformation, or enterprise platform modernization.
Demonstrated expertise in Private Markets operating models and large-scale technology implementations.

Success Measures

The Managing Director Will Be Measured On

Advancement of the Private Equity platform strategy and roadmap.
Improvement in operational efficiency and automation.
Enhanced Investran platform adoption and governance.
Reduction of operational risk and production incidents.
Increased platform scalability and standardization.
Delivery of transformation initiatives on scope, budget, and timeline.
Improved client and employee experience.

Salary Range

$170,000 - $267,500 Annual

The range quoted above applies to the role in the primary location specified. If the candidate would ultimately work outside of the primary location above, the applicable range could differ.

Employees are eligible to participate in State Street’s comprehensive benefits program, which includes: our retirement savings plan (401K) with company match; insurance coverage including basic life, medical, dental, vision, long-term disability, and other optional additional coverages; paid-time off including vacation, sick leave, short term disability, and family care responsibilities; access to our Employee Assistance Program; incentive compensation including eligibility for annual performance-based awards (excluding certain sales roles subject to sales incentive plans); and, eligibility for certain tax advantaged savings plans.

We are committed to fostering an environment where every employee feels valued and empowered to reach their full potential. jobs.title: Director, Financial Planning, Analysis and Corporate Reporting
jobs.description:
About our Client:
Build Canada Homes was established by the Government of Canada in September 2025 to scale up the delivery of affordable housing across the country. Its mandate is to increase housing supply by bringing together public land, flexible financing, and development expertise to deliver more affordable and non-market housing where it is needed most.

As a federal Crown corporation, BCH was created to respond to the scale and urgency of Canada’s housing challenge. It builds on existing federal capacity while introducing a more coordinated, delivery-focused approach—working in partnership across the housing system to move projects forward and deliver results for Canadians.

This role is offers a hybrid model. They currently work 2-3 days in office and potentially 4 days in the future.

Position Scope:

The Director, Financial Planning, Analysis and Corporate Reporting lead the delivery, coordination, and continuous improvement of financial planning, analysis, budgeting, forecasting, and corporate reporting activities across Build Canada Homes and its subsidiaries (collectively, the “Corporation” or “BCH”). The role is responsible for managing financial planning cycles, consolidating budget and forecast inputs, preparing financial analyses and performance reports, and delivering timely, accurate financial information that informs operational planning, resource allocation, funding decisions, and organizational performance monitoring.

The role collaborates with internal and external stakeholders to coordinate financial inputs, monitor results, analyze variances, prepare reporting materials, and maintain alignment with established financial policies, controls, reporting requirements, and governance expectations. The Director, Financial Planning, Analysis and Corporate Reporting role applies financial expertise to manage planning processes, identify financial risks and operational issues, improve reporting practices, and deliver reliable analysis within the assigned scope of Corporate Services and Corporate Finance, Treasury & Reporting.

Responsibilities:

FINANCIAL PLANNING, BUDGETING & FORECASTING

Leads the coordination and delivery of BCH’s budgeting, forecasting, and financial planning processes within assigned scope.
Develops planning calendars, templates, assumptions, and submission requirements to promote consistent and timely financial inputs.
Consolidates financial plans, forecasts, and budget submissions from internal stakeholders to prepare integrated financial outlooks.
Analyzes funding requirements, resource needs, and cost drivers to inform operational planning and funding allocation.
Performs sensitivity analysis and financial modelling.
Provides financial advice and interpretation to internal stakeholders on budget assumptions, planning inputs, cost pressures, and financial trends.

CORPORATE REPORTING, ANALYSIS, & PERFORMANCE INSIGHTS

Leads the preparation of financial reports, dashboards, briefing materials, variance analyses, and decision-support information for leadership review.
Prepares corporate reporting materials related to financial performance, funding, cost trends, and resource utilization.
Translates complex financial information into concise reports and presentations that support management review and operational decision-making.
Develops and maintains financial models, planning tools, and reporting templates to improve efficiency and analytical quality.

FINANCIAL CONTROLS, COMPLIANCE & CONTINUOUS IMPROVEMENT

Leads and supervises the team responsible for the accurate and timely recording of all corporate financial transactions, including corporate operating expenditures, capital expenditures, journal entries, and general ledger activities
Oversees month-end, quarter-end, and year-end accounting close processes, ensuring completeness, accuracy, and compliance with accounting standards and organizational policies.
Identifies and addresses financial control issues, reporting risks, data quality concerns, and process gaps, escalating matters where required.
Leads the annual external financial statements audit and coordinates with finance, corporate services, legal, auditors and other stakeholders to support financial reporting, compliance and regulatory requirements.
Leads continuous improvement of accounting, financial planning, analysis, reporting, and performance management processes to enhance efficiency, accuracy, transparency, and decision support.
Evaluates financial reporting processes to identify opportunities for automation, standardization, improved controls and reduce manual effort as BCH’s operating model evolves.

Qualifications and Experience:

Post-secondary degree or diploma in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, Commerce, Economics, or a related field.
Professional accounting or finance designation, such as CPA, CFA, or an equivalent designation.
Minimum 5-10 years of experience in financial planning and analysis, budgeting, forecasting, corporate reporting, management reporting, accounting, or related finance roles.
Experience leading financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, analysis, and reporting in a complex organization.
Experience preparing financial reports, dashboards, and briefing materials for senior leadership.
Experience managing teams, priorities, timelines, and deliverables.
Knowledge of accounting, financial controls, budgeting, reporting, and performance management.
Knowledge of real estate, housing, construction, investments, or corporate finance is an asset.
Experience working with internal and external stakeholders, including auditors and regulators.
Strong analytical, financial modelling, communication, and stakeholder management skills.
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office; experience with ERP, financial planning, and reporting systems is an asset.

Compensation:
$132,163 - $165,203 base salary, Discretionary bonus, Health, Dental, Vision, Vacation, Personal days, Employee Family Assistance Program, Fitness Allowance, Defined Contribution Pension

jobs.title: Head of VCF Professional Services Portfolio - Americas
jobs.description:
Job Description:

Division Overview

The VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) Division empowers enterprise organizations globally to run mission-critical and modern workloads on a secure, resilient, and cost-effective platform. Built upon core innovations like VMware vSphere alongside vSAN, NSX, and Aria, our private cloud solutions deliver the scalability and agility of public cloud environments while maintaining strict security, predictable TCO, and performance control. Our cross-functional teams spanning product development, marketing, professional services, and customer support collaborate to drive digital transformation across key industries including financial services, healthcare, manufacturing, education, and government.

Job Description & Key Responsibilities

We are seeking an experienced leader to direct the development and go-to-market (GTM) execution for the VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) Professional Services portfolio across the Americas region. In this role, you will align service offerings with product roadmaps and regional sales strategies to support over $500M in annual services revenue.

Key Responsibilities:

Portfolio & GTM Strategy: Drive the end-to-end strategy for VCF and VMware Kubernetes Services Professional Services offerings across the Americas, aligning portfolio development with sales goals and product direction.
Executive Alignment: Collaborate directly with Americas Sales and Services executive leadership (SVP level) to set regional priorities, boost services attach rates, and unblock high-value enterprise sales opportunities.
Governance & Leadership: Guide and mentor Services Scoping Architects and technical leads while establishing standardized pre-sales qualification, scoping governance, and consultative deal structuring.
Sales & Field Enablement: Design and deliver enablement initiatives for technical pre-sales, core account teams, and internal services staff focused on services selling and consumption growth.
Partner Ecosystem Growth: Assist with developing partner delivery capabilities and regional practice capacity across professional services offerings.
Evangelism: Deliver internal and external presentations to stakeholders at various levels.

Minimum Requirements

Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience in Enterprise Software, Cloud Infrastructure, or IT Professional Services.
12+ years related experience required
Extensive background in professional services portfolio management, GTM strategy, or technical pre-sales leadership.

Deep technical and business knowledge of VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF), VMware Kubernetes Services, and modern private/hybrid cloud architecture.
Proven ability to partner effectively with executive leadership (SVP level) and lead technical scoping and architecture teams.

Master of Business Administration (MBA) highly preferred.
Demonstrated experience presenting at enterprise technology events (e.g., VMware Explore).

jobs.title: VP, Enterprise Sales
jobs.description:
About CoLab

At CoLab, we help mechanical engineering teams bring life-changing products to market years sooner.

We build AI for engineers designing cars, medical devices, and jet engines. Products this complex aren't sketched and sent to production. Teams spend months on iterations, reviews, and tests, predicting how every part performs before anything is built. CoLab is where those reviews happen, and we capture the rationale behind every change. Other tools show what changed between versions. Only CoLab knows why. That's how our AI helps manufacturers like Bobcat, Triumph Motorcycles, and GE Appliances make better decisions, eliminate rework cycles, and get to market faster.

Proudly based in St. John's, Newfoundland, CoLab started with one customer in 2018. Since then we've raised a $72M Series C, been named the 57th fastest growing company in North America by Deloitte (Fast 500™), signed multi-year AI partnerships with companies like Bombardier, and grown to a team of 250+.

About the Role

CoLab is hiring a highly motivated VP of Enterprise Sales to scale our enterprise sales team and the process behind it during a critical phase of growth. You will report to our SVP of Sales and lead enterprise teams, whose Account Executives sell deals from $25K to $500K and upwards of $1M to Fortune 500 manufacturers in automotive, industrial, heavy machinery, medical device and consumer products.

CoLab sells into engineering and design teams, not just procurement or supply chain. These are complex, multi-stakeholder deals with long cycles and no pre-existing budget line, so this person needs to be a strong closer and a stronger coach.

What you'll do

You will own enterprise new-logo and expansion revenue and build the repeatable system that lets the team scale.

Lead and coach enterprise teams.
Run a weekly coaching cadence, review deals in depth, and sit in on key calls to raise how reps run complex, multi-threaded cycles.
Recruit, develop, and retain top talent.
Provide effective coaching, career development, and performance management, and set clear expectations and scorecards.
Own the number.
Set quotas and territories, drive pipeline coverage, and deliver an accurate forecast to the SVP of Sales.
Inspect and refine the sales process.
Dive into the pipeline, drive daily improvements, and enforce consistent stage criteria, mutual action plans, and deal reviews using a methodology such as MEDDPICC.
Be a hands-on player/coach.
Lead by example: jump on intro calls, step into enterprise negotiations, and help close the largest accounts.
Expand within existing customers.
Identify upsell and cross-sell opportunities to grow business with the current client base.
Sell value to engineering buyers.
Help reps build business cases around design error cost, review cycle time, and quality, and engage engineering leaders and executive sponsors.
Collaborate cross-functionally.
Work with BDRs and Marketing on pipeline and account targeting, and Customer Engineering and Product on technical selling.
Report with accuracy.
Use Salesforce (and other tools) to report sales performance, pipeline movement, and forecasts to the senior leadership team.
Share market feedback and experiment.
Monitor customer, market, and competitor activity, feed insights to internal partners, and test new sales strategies to improve ARR and sales efficiency.

What you'll bring

10+ years of B2B SaaS sales, including 4+ years leading enterprise sales teams (Director or VP level), ideally with experience multiple teams and managers ( frontline managers to Director).
A track record of closing six-figure deals, ideally $500K+ and up to $1M, with multiple stakeholders and long sales cycles.
Experience selling into technical buyers and complex organizations, using consultative methods in undefined product categories where educating the buyer and creating budget is essential.
Experience scaling a sales organization through a high-growth phase and building process that outlasts you.
Strong executive presence and the ability to build trust quickly with skeptical C-suite and VP-level stakeholders.
A disciplined forecaster with a working command of Salesforce and a formal methodology (MEDDPICC, Challenger, or similar), and the judgment to adapt it.
A coach first: you can step into an existing team of experienced reps and earn credibility by improving how they sell, including in remote or hybrid environments.
A builder's mindset: you see what's missing, create it, and don't wait for a playbook or permission.
No ego, high drive, and a fast learner who seeks feedback and works well cross-functionally. Values of Kindness & Respect, One Team One Mission, and Better Everyday come naturally.

Nice to have

Experience selling into manufacturing, aerospace and defense, automotive, or industrial customers, and comfort with engineering buyers (CAD, PLM, design review).
Experience selling AI, engineering software, or design-collaboration tools.
Experience selling a mix of SaaS, services, and hardware.
Prior experience inheriting an established team, not only building one from scratch.
Familiarity with Salesforce, Gong, and a modern sales-tech stack.

Why CoLab and the details

This is a chance to lead the enterprise sales team at a company already selling complex deals to Fortune 500 manufacturers, at a critical phase of growth. You will shape the team, the process, and how CoLab sells to engineering organizations.

Frequently cited statistics show that people who identify with historically marginalized groups are likely to apply to jobs only if they meet 100% of the qualifications. We encourage you to help us break that statistic and apply even if you don't meet every single qualification—your potential is what matters most to us.

jobs.title: Director, Treasury and Accounts Payable
jobs.description:
About our Client:
Build Canada Homes was established by the Government of Canada in September 2025 to scale up the delivery of affordable housing across the country. Its mandate is to increase housing supply by bringing together public land, flexible financing, and development expertise to deliver more affordable and non-market housing where it is needed most.

As a federal Crown corporation, BCH was created to respond to the scale and urgency of Canada’s housing challenge. It builds on existing federal capacity while introducing a more coordinated, delivery-focused approach—working in partnership across the housing system to move projects forward and deliver results for Canadians.

This role is offers a hybrid model. They currently work 2-3 days in office and potentially 4 days in the future.

Position Scope:

The Director, Treasury and Accounts Payable is responsible for leading and overseeing treasury administration and reporting activities as well as Accounts payable operations across Build Canada Homes and its subsidiaries (collectively, the “Corporation” or “BCH”). The role manages statutory funding requests from the shareholder, cash flows forecasts and reporting, cash administration activities, banking operations, treasury reporting, payment processing, supplier and employee disbursements, and associated financial controls to ensure the timely, accurate, and compliant execution of financial transactions. Through operational oversight, functional expertise, and team leadership, the role supports effective cash management, vendor relationships, financial stewardship, and service delivery.

The role collaborates with internal and external stakeholders to coordinate financial operations and support organizational priorities. The role contributes to operational planning and implementation, monitors performance, supports financial reporting activities, manages operational and financial risks within its area of responsibility, and ensures compliance with applicable policies, controls, and regulatory requirements. The role identifies opportunities to improve processes, systems, and service delivery while maintaining accountability for achieving operational objectives and delivering results.

Responsibilities:

TREASURY MANAGEMENT & CASH ADMINISTRATION

Coordinates the statutory funding requests from the shareholder, including gathering financial information from internal parties, preparing the statutory funding package, and liaising with the shareholder’s groups.
Administers treasury activities, including cash positioning, liquidity monitoring, banking administration, and cash movement processes.
Develops cash flow forecasting, liquidity planning, and treasury reporting activities.
Supports investment administration activities and treasury-related financial analysis as required.
Identifies, assesses, and mitigates treasury-related operational and financial risks through effective controls and monitoring activities.
Maintains banking documentation, signing authorities, and treasury procedures to support operational effectiveness and compliance.

ACCOUNTS PAYABLE OPERATIONS & CONTROLS

Leads and oversees end-to-end accounts payable operations, ensuring the accurate, timely, and compliant processing of supplier payments, employee expense reimbursements, holdbacks, sales taxes, and other disbursements.
Supervises accounts payable resources, establishes work priorities, allocates work, monitors service levels, and provides coaching and performance feedback.
Ensures compliance with delegated authorities, financial controls, regulatory requirements, and organizational policies, including supporting and/or leading reviews or audits (i.e., sales tax).
Resolves complex payment, vendor, and transaction issues while maintaining effective stakeholder relationships.

FINANCIAL COMPLIANCE, REPORTING & CONTINOUS IMPROVEMENT

Supports monthly, quarterly, and annual financial reporting processes through the preparation and review of accounts payable and treasury information, reconciliations, and analyses.
Monitors operational performance and prepares reports, analyses, and recommendations to support informed decision-making.
Develops, maintains, and updates procedures, controls, and process documentation to support consistency, transparency, and compliance.
Supports budget planning, operational forecasting, and financial management activities within the functional area

Qualifications and Experience:

Post-secondary degree or diploma in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, Commerce, or a related discipline.
CPA designation (or other relevant designation) is required
Minimum 7–10 years of progressive experience in, treasury, accounting, or financial operations environments.
Experience managing treasury operations, banking relationships, accounts payable, payments, and financial controls.
Experience leading teams and providing operational leadership in a finance environment.
Experience supporting audits, financial reporting, reconciliations, and compliance activities.
Experience with statutory funding requests and banking draws is an asset.
Experience in real estate, construction, investment, or other complex operating environments is an asset.
Strong knowledge of treasury, cash management, accounts payable, financial reporting, and internal controls.
Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel; experience with ERP, treasury, payment, and financial reporting systems is an asset.
Strong knowledge of treasury operations, banking processes, cash management principles, accounts payable practices, and internal controls.
Knowledge of financial reporting requirements, accounting practices, and compliance obligations.

Compensation:
$132,163 - $165,203 base salary, Discretionary bonus, Health, Dental, Vision, Vacation, Personal days, Employee Family Assistance Program, Fitness Allowance, Defined Contribution Pension

AI Disclosure:
AI will not be used in the recruitment process.

Vacancy Disclosure:
This is a new role.

jobs.description:
The Opportunity

Crescent Oral Surgery (COS)
is seeking a dynamic and experienced Practice Director
to join our growing team. This full-time leadership role spans across our three locations in Toronto, Aurora, and Richmond Hill
, and plays a critical part in the ongoing growth and operational excellence of our practices.

Reporting to the Partners
, the Practice Director
will oversee all aspects of day-to-day operations, contribute strategically to our growth initiatives, and lead a team of over 90 professionals. This position will collaborate closely with internal team leads, referral networks, and industry partners, ensuring the delivery of exceptional patient care while driving operational and financial success.

Crescent Oral Surgery
is a leading oral and maxillofacial surgery practice with a strong provincial and national reputation. Our multidisciplinary team of nine Surgeons, two Oral Medicine Specialists, a Radiologist, and a Pain Specialist is dedicated to delivering expert care with professionalism and compassion.

Who You Are

You are a strategic, hands-on healthcare leader who thrives on balancing operational rigour with a genuine commitment to people and patients.
With a proven record in senior leadership, you are equally comfortable owning a P&L, guiding department heads, and building trusted relationships with surgeons, referral partners, and team members.
You lead change with clarity and confidence, bring structure to complex, multi-site environments, and use data to make smart decisions that drive growth.
Collaborative, approachable, and accountable, you inspire high-performing teams and are energized by the opportunity to shape the future of a respected oral surgery practice.

In This Role, You Will

Operational & Financial Excellence

Manage clinic financials, including overseeing profit and loss, revenue forecasting, and labor cost management.
Ensure regular on-site presence at each practice location, to monitor performance and support all staff in delivering high-quality patient care and experiences.
Lead monthly, quarterly, and annual business reviews and communicate key metrics to stakeholders.
Collaborate to develop an annual COS budget reflective of the annual growth strategy.
Develop and execute strategies to optimize daily operations across all COS locations.
Oversee procurement processes and coordinate material and resource allocation
Oversee IT operations and systems efficiencies, as well as consistent governance, reporting, and process optimization.

Leading People and Building Strong Relationships

Lead and mentor department heads, providing strategic direction, coaching, and support.
Foster a positive, collaborative, and high-performance culture aligned with COS values.
Support associates in building their practices and expanding referral relationships.
Guide goal setting and performance management processes to drive continuous improvement.
Identify talent development opportunities and contribute to succession planning efforts.
Ensure operational alignment between clinical, administrative, coordination, and call center teams through effective team leadership and engagement efforts.
Collaborate with Dentalcorp departments (HR, Compliance, DC Learning) to maintain regulatory compliance and training standards.
Build a strong network and culture across all three practice locations, with Team Leads, Team Members, Associates, Partners, Patients, and the Dental Community at-large as an ambassador for COS.

Patient Care and Experience

Ensure the utmost quality care outcomes for patients, through required compliance training and standards for all COS practices and team members.
Identify, develop, and lead innovative initiatives and improvements to continuously enhance the patient experience, alongside COS Partners and team members.
Work closely with team leads, surgeons, and Dentalcorp support teams to resolve patient concerns and maintain high satisfaction levels.

Transformation and Growth

Develop and oversee the annual growth strategy for COS, including call centre and referral strategy, marketing, talent management, and other growth levers and opportunities
Leverage data insights and identify innovative solutions to drive growth opportunities across all marketing efforts.
Design and implement an annual growth strategy including referral development, marketing, and talent acquisition.
Align strategy with operational implementation to ensure successful outcomes between clinical, admin, and call centre teams across COS practices and community referral practices.

What You’ll Bring

Bachelor's and/or Master’s Degree in Business Administration, Healthcare Management or a related field is required.
Proven experience in Senior Leadership Roles, with Advanced Operational and People Management responsibilities is required.
Demonstrated ability to lead change, manage multiple projects, and build strong cross-functional relationships.
Strong strategic thinking, commercial awareness, and execution capabilities.
Strong financial and business acumen, including experience managing P&L, forecasting, budgeting, and performance metrics.
A track record of driving measurable, sustainable growth through operational discipline and KPI management
Excellent leadership, communication, and collaboration skills, with the ability to build strong relationships across functions and levels
Experience leading cross-functional initiatives and executing complex projects with multiple stakeholders
Strong organizational skills, sound judgment, and the ability to manage multiple priorities effectively
A valid driver’s license and access to a vehicle, with the flexibility to travel within Ontario, including occasional overnight stays

Why Dentalcorp?

Dentalcorp
is North America’s leading and fastest-growing network of dental practices. Through industry-leading technology, expertise, and scale, we help practices grow while supporting dental professionals to retain their clinical autonomy. Here, you’ll be trusted with meaningful responsibility, supported to grow, and surrounded by people who share ideas and raise the bar together. Our Beyond Brilliant
values— Beyond the Status Quo
, Beyond Excellence
, Brilliant Together
, and Brilliant Experiences
—guide how we innovate, collaborate, deliver, and put people at the centre. 

The salary range for this position is $120,000.00 CAD to $140,000.00 CAD annually (plus a bonus of up to 20% and competitive total rewards and benefits package). Offers within this range are determined based on relevant experience, skills, and qualifications, as well as internal equity considerations. This job posting is for an existing vacancy. 

Candidates must be legally eligible to work in Canada. At Dentalcorp, we recognize that inclusivity and diversity strengthen our culture and make us better. We are committed to ensuring that the talent we hire is reflective of the diverse communities and patients we serve. To ensure equal opportunity for all candidates, we strongly encourage applicants requiring an accommodation to let their recruiter know during the recruitment/selection process. We appreciate all applicants for taking the time to apply, however, only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

new_jobs.title: Senior Director, Enterprise Architecture - Corporate Technology Services
new_jobs.description:
Accelerate your success at Colliers.

Why Colliers?

As one of Canada’s leading commercial real estate services firms, we are driven by our mission to accelerate success for our people, clients, and communities.

A career at Colliers gives you the opportunity to make an impact, advance your career, and collaborate with top-tier talent. Don’t just take our word for it – we’ve been recognized as a top employer on a number of prestigious lists, including Best Workplaces in Canada, Best Workplaces with Most Trusted Executive Teams, among others.

Toronto, ON / Vancouver, BC, Hybrid

About The Role

As Global Domain Enterprise Architect, Corporate Technology Systems within our Global Enterprise Architecture organization, you’ll define the global architectural direction for the technology platforms supporting Colliers’ corporate functions. You’ll partner with business and technology leaders to simplify and modernize our global technology landscape, establish scalable standards, and ensure major technology investments translate into sustainable business outcomes. Support global time zones: Work closely with stakeholders across Pacific and APAC regions, with flexibility to adjust working hours on most days as business needs require.

Lead global enterprise architecture: Define current-state, target-state, and transition architectures, roadmaps, principles, and standards across ERP, Finance, HCM, Procurement, CRM/MarTech, Legal, Risk & Compliance, ECM, and other corporate platforms.
Drive modernization and simplification: Lead application portfolio rationalization and recommend where platforms should be standardized, modernized, consolidated, replaced, or retired to reduce technical debt and complexity.
Shape strategic technology investments: Provide architecture leadership for major transformation initiatives, evaluating SaaS and enterprise platforms against business value, integration, data, security, scalability, total cost, and long-term strategic fit.
Advance AI, data, and integration strategy: Establish scalable patterns for enterprise data, APIs, integration, automation, AI, identity, and shared services while embedding security, privacy, governance, and regulatory requirements.
Collaborate across the global enterprise: Partner with senior business leaders, Product, Data & AI, Cloud & DevOps, Cybersecurity, Integration, Legal, Procurement, Risk, and strategic vendors to turn architecture strategy into executable outcomes.

What You Bring

Education: Degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, Business, or a related discipline preferred.
12+ years of relevant experience: Significant experience in enterprise architecture, domain architecture, technology strategy, or large-scale transformation within complex global or federated organizations.
Enterprise platform architecture expertise: Demonstrated experience architecting and modernizing complex technology portfolios, including experience across at least two of the following three domains: Finance/ERP, HR/HCM, and CRM/MarTech.
Strong technical and transformation expertise: Deep understanding of SaaS platforms, application rationalization, enterprise integration, APIs, data architecture, cloud, cybersecurity, identity, AI/automation, and executable transition roadmaps.
Executive influence and communication: Proven ability to advise senior executives, challenge vendor and solution assumptions, and translate complex architectural decisions into clear business outcomes while remaining technically credible with architecture and engineering teams.

What We Offer

Innovative projects:
Work on cutting-edge initiatives that shape our communities, drive our growth, and make a tangible impact.

Career growth:
Advance your career and achieve your goals with industry-leading training and development programs.

Competitive benefits & compensation:
Enjoy a comprehensive and flexible benefits package along with competitive compensation that rewards your contributions and supports your well-being.

Collaborative culture:
Join our enterprising team where innovation thrives, collaboration is key, and our people are empowered to be their authentic selves and do their best work.

Diversity, Equity & Inclusion:
Our robust North American Diversity & Inclusion Program features eight Employee Resource Groups (ERGs), where you can connect, learn, and contribute to a diverse and supportive community. Learn more: https://www.collierscanada.com/en-ca/careers/diversity-and-inclusion

Global network
: Join a global team of 28,000 professionals across 70 countries, where you'll expand your network and learn from experts in a dynamic international community. Accelerate your career and enhance your expertise as you connect and collaborate with top talent around the world.

Applicants must be currently authorized to work in Canada on a full-time basis. The employer will not sponsor applicants for work visas.

Direct applicants only please, no agencies.

Colliers encourages applications from all qualified individuals and will accommodate applicants' disability-related needs, up to the point of undue hardship, throughout all stages of the recruitment and selection process.
